Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast Top NBA media day headlines LeBron says he envisioned joining Knicks as free agent | Philly stars ready to 'sacrifice' Clippers apologize to fans, vow to move past investigation | Ingram (Achilles) out Edwards happy to cede Wolves' PG duties to Ball Wizards, AD to wait until summer for extension talks Karl-Anthony Towns wants extension to stay with Knicks Jokic on his next Nuggets deal: 'I'm going to sign next year' Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' Sept. 28 Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path' When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers . But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day. "He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that." LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." James and the 76ers will play the Knicks at the Garden on opening night, Oct. 20. No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors." Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. Sept. 26 Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday. 2026 NBA offseason trade grades Sept. 25 What's next for Curry and the Warriors? Stephen Curry 's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings. The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer. By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million. For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer. Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski . The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. "[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump." Grizzlies waive Russell The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

What worked (and didn't) in 12 NBA season debuts: LeBron, LaMelo, more stars
teamStories.summary: Which stars shined with their new teams? Which might want a do-over? Ben Golliver examines 12 opening week debuts.
teamStories.detailText: Newly minted Portland Trail Blazers guard Ja Morant said it best Wednesday: "You only get one chance at a first impression." Though the Blazers were one of several teams to ace their season openers, there were also plenty of stars who might want a do-over. After all, Jayson Tatum 's Boston Celtics blew a 22-point lead to the Pistons, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama shot 1-for-13 in a loss to the rival Oklahoma City Thunder , and Giannis Antetokounmpo 's Miami Heat were blown off their home court by the Minnesota Timberwolves . Let's run through the NBA's opening-week action -- through Thursday, every team will have played at least once -- with an eye toward the first impressions made by key players suiting up for new teams this season. Which ones launched with ease, and which succumbed to false starts? Jump to a season debut Great: Kawhi | Dame | Kessler | OKC starting 5 Good: LaMelo | LeBron | AD | PG-13 | Garland Rough: Giannis | Yaxel vs. Luka | Miles Bridges Great first impressions Kawhi Leonard , Raptors The schedule-makers gifted Leonard a home opener against the lowly Chicago Bulls on Wednesday, and the two-time Finals MVP took full advantage. Leonard wasted no time moving past a tumultuous summer marked by a delayed trade and the NBA's lengthy salary cap circumvention investigation, enjoying a hearty welcome back from the Toronto crowd before scoring 23 points and snagging four steals in a blowout victory. The scariest part for East rivals: Leonard didn't have his signature midrange jumper dialed in and played only 24 minutes, yet the Raptors still managed a 43-point margin of victory that tied for the fifth largest in franchise history. Toronto ran up the score with excellent balance across its starting lineup, as Leonard, Scottie Barnes , RJ Barrett and Immanuel Quickley each surpassed 20 points. How high can Leonard lift an offense that ranked 15th last season? Damian Lillard , Trail Blazers The Blazers' icon spent Wednesday putting his career back on track after a forgettable two-year detour with the Bucks and an Achilles injury that sidelined him last season. In his first game for Portland since 2023, the nine-time All-Star guard provided such an emotional jolt that the Blazers stormed out to a preposterous 21-0 lead and cruised to a 124-83 blowout of the Phoenix Suns . No one will argue with the results from the opener, but it remains an open question whether Lillard and Morant are the ideal starting backcourt for Portland. Against Phoenix, Lillard scored 25 points and hit six 3-pointers, and Morant added 14 points and eight assists in only 23 minutes. Tougher tests await: The Suns lack big and physical perimeter playmakers capable of exploiting Portland's undersized guards. But it's nice to see Lillard back where he belongs in Rip City. Walker Kessler , Lakers Well, it's hard to beat perfect. Kessler made all 12 of his shots, including 10 dunks, and grabbed nine rebounds in the Lakers' blowout of the Warriors on Wednesday. Not bad for a guy playing in his first regular-season game since last October and in his first game for the Lakers since arriving from the Jazz in a summer sign-and-trade deal. After only one game, Kessler already looks like the best center Luka Doncic has played with in his nine-year career. "Inside the NBA'''s Shaquille O'Neal went even further, opining that Kessler is "the best big man in the NBA." Slow down, Shaq: The Lakers' smashing debut came against an injury-plagued Warriors team that rolled over after halftime. Still, Kessler earned praise from Lakers coach JJ Redick for his ability to change ends quickly. The 7-foot-2 center clearly understands that his gigantic frame won't do him any good if he's stuck trailing the action. If Kessler can put together a complete season from a health standpoint and continue to serve as a constant vertical target, then Doncic will be a major factor in the MVP discussion. Thunder starters Technically, Oklahoma City's most important newcomer has been Aday Mara , a 7-foot-3 rookie center who made quite the splash in his NBA debut by swatting Wembanyama at the rim. But the Thunder also trotted out a tweaked starting lineup after trading longtime starter Luguentz Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a cost-cutting move this summer. Cason Wallace stepped into Dort's sport, filling out an imposing group that includes two-time MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , All-Stars Jalen Williams and Chet Holmgren and center Isaiah Hartenstein . In a convincing road win over San Antonio on Tuesday, the Thunder starters exhibited excellent discipline and togetherness while frustrating Wembanyama from start to finish. Two days later, Oklahoma City overcame poor outside shooting to put away another top West challenger: Nikola Jokic's Denver Nuggets . Oklahoma City also got key boosts from Mara, guard Jared McCain and veteran stopper Alex Caruso this week. With Williams healthy, it's not too early to ask whether Oklahoma City's rotation is actually better than the 2025 championship team and last season's group that led the league with 64 wins. Good first impressions LaMelo Ball , Timberwolves Ball did his part to position the Timberwolves as lightning rods by shuffling a good 10 feet without incurring a traveling violation while launching a step-back 3-pointer against the Heat. Clips of his comical sidestepping immediately went viral, prompting the NBA referees' association to clarify on social media that an infraction had occurred: "[Ball] takes four steps after gathering the ball and travels." Detractors will paint Ball's looseness as evidence that the modern NBA game has slipped into a less serious endeavor, while proponents will point out that Ball's new partnership with Anthony Edwards is wildly fun. Both sides make valid points, but the loud and brash Timberwolves can't be dismissed as frivolous after absolutely wrecking the new-look Heat in Miami. Edwards took full advantage of playing alongside a primetime backcourt playmaker for the first time in his seven-year career. The four-time All-Star went off for 45 points to handily win the superstar showdown against Miami's Antetokounmpo. Based solely on the first 72 hours of the season, Minnesota has a strong case as the NBA's most watchable team. LeBron James , Philadelphia 76ers The best compliment that can be paid to James for his early work in Philadelphia is that the 76ers still feel like Tyrese Maxey 's team. Maxey posted team highs in points and shot attempts as the 76ers spoiled the New York Knicks ' ring night celebrations Tuesday and came back to defeat the Cavaliers on Thursday. So far, James, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid have all sacrificed their individual numbers as the star-studded roster continues to acclimate. James found a variety of ways to be helpful against the Knicks: He lined up Brown for a buzzer-beating 3-pointer on an inbounds play, he shifted up to defend centers when Embiid encountered foul trouble, and he helped Philadelphia rack up 24 fast-break points as both a distributor and a finisher. Down the stretch against Cleveland, he made way for Embiid and Brown as Philadelphia put the finishing touches on a 29-point rally. Though James hasn't found his outside stroke and has displayed occasional lapses of defensive intensity, his ability to organize an offense and manage game flow are crucial additions for Philadelphia. Given the scope of their offseason changes, the 76ers have looked ahead of schedule. Anthony Davis , Wizards Davis catapulted the overhauled Wizards to an opening-night win over the rebuilding Milwaukee Bucks with 34 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and two steals. Lest anyone overlook his handiwork, Davis poked fun at Washington's home attendance woes. "I'd like it to be a little more packed in here," he said. "Even when I was here last year, [for] the very first home game, it was 'Dress Like a Seat' night in here." Though Davis and the Wizards remain an awkward and uncertain partnership given his lack of a contract extension, the 10-time All-Star's production and humor are welcome additions to a franchise that has had little to offer its long-suffering fans in recent years. The next step for Washington: incorporate No. 1 pick AJ Dybantsa , who sat out the opener because of an ankle injury. Trae Young kept everyone involved with 13 assists against Milwaukee, but Dybantsa's return is bound to shake up Washington's shot distribution in a major way. Paul George , Celtics During his short-lived and somewhat ill-fated two-year run with the 76ers, George scored at least 38 points only once in 78 games. Wouldn't you know it? The nine-time All-Star hit that mark and drilled seven 3-pointers in his Celtics debut Tuesday. Unfortunately for George, the Pistons pulled off an epic second-half comeback to spoil his debut. Boston was undone by Tatum's poor outside shooting and inability to get to the free throw line, and the offense's lengthy cold stretch against Detroit's imposing defense. Caution is in order when it comes to assessing George's sparkling opener. Though he's a clear fit in an offense that thrives by generating 3-pointers, Boston probably can't count on the 36-year-old forward to generate rim pressure and a high volume of free throws on a nightly basis. Tatum remains the Celtics' best answer to those needs. Darius Garland , Clippers Most of the hoopla in Los Angeles this week belonged to Doncic and the Lakers, but Garland deserves kudos for carrying the injury-ravaged Clippers to a win over the Sacramento Kings on opening night. Garland, 26, downshifted as a scorer once he was paired with Donovan Mitchell on the Cavaliers, but the Clippers need him to crank it all the way up as they cope with the absences of Brandon Ingram , Max Strus and Bradley Beal . Garland delivered by scoring 30 points and easily outplaying Sacramento rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr . After that soft launch against a Kings team that might finish in the Western Conference's basement, Garland must lead the Clippers through a schedule gauntlet that includes two head-to-head games against the Lakers, trips to Oklahoma City, Minnesota and Golden State, and a much-anticipated showdown with Leonard's Raptors over the next two weeks. Gulp. Rough first impressions Giannis Antetokounmpo, Heat New home, same problems? That's the nagging question for Antetokounmpo, who posted 35 points and six assists in 30 minutes but couldn't stop the Heat from getting waxed by the Timberwolves. Antetokounmpo orchestrated an exit from Milwaukee because the Bucks had fallen far behind the East's top contenders, but his new supporting cast in Miami didn't exactly rise to the occasion Wednesday. Cold outside shooting, an unremarkable showing from Bam Adebayo and a troubling defensive performance all contributed to an embarrassing loss. The Heat should look better against some softer opponents on their upcoming schedule, but their offense won't be able to keep up unless Antetokounmpo and the Heat can get better results from his drive-and-kick passing. The two-time MVP had only one assist against three turnovers against Minnesota, and Miami's 8-for-33 showing from deep just won't get it done against serious competition. Yaxel Lendeborg , Warriors Lendeborg's NBA career is one game old, but he's already mounting a strong effort to supplant teammate Draymond Green as the NBA's biggest yapper. During Golden State's 127-105 opening loss to the Lakers, Lendeborg was hit with a technical foul for repeatedly exchanging words with Doncic. Afterward, the 24-year-old forward said he "lost all respect" for Doncic because of his "whining and complaining." Lendeborg's unfiltered and often insightful musings prompted genuine laughter from the assembled media in Los Angeles, but he would do well to pace himself in front of the microphones. After leading the University of Michigan to an NCAA title last season, Lendeborg joined the Warriors as a lottery pick and promptly led the franchise to the Las Vegas summer league title. Unfortunately, Golden State's regular season is shaping up to be much more challenging. The Warriors lack consistent scoring aside from star Stephen Curry , and their undermanned frontcourt was overwhelmed by the Lakers. This could be a long season in the Bay Area, and Lendeborg will inevitably face backlash if he continues to speak so frankly about rival stars after losses. Miles Bridges , Suns Suns owner Mat Ishbia has a well-known history of bringing in players and executives with ties to his alma mater, Michigan State, but his latest Spartan addition is off to a rocky start. Bridges, who was acquired in an offseason trade with Charlotte, scored only eight points on 3-of-11 shooting in Phoenix's loss to Portland. The Blazers outscored the Suns by 35 points in the veteran forward's 29 minutes. Some patience is needed given that Bridges and center Khaman Maluach were both new additions to coach Jordan Ott's starting lineup. Even so, Bridges must prove he's capable of bringing more grit to a Phoenix team that was mauled 56-39 on the glass in the opener. The Suns are counting on Bridges, who holds a $22.8 million expiring contract, to shape up because they parted with their 2033 first-round pick in the deal with the Hornets. If Bridges doesn't prove to be a long-term difference-maker, Phoenix will have squandered another prime draft asset.

stories.title: 49ers WR Evans, DE Bosa, WR Samuel out vs. Atlanta; WR Kirk may return
stories.summary: 49ers receivers Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr., and defensive end Nick Bosa are among a half dozen players who have been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Falcons.
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- With a bye week coming soon, San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans and defensive end Nick Bosa won't play in Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons as they deal with Achilles tendinitis and a calf injury, respectively. On Friday, the Niners ruled Evans and Bosa out against the Falcons after neither player participated in practice this week. In addition to Bosa and Evans, the Niners also ruled out wideout Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring), linebackers Luke Gifford (groin) and Garret Wallow (hamstring) and safety Marques Sigle (ankle). Coach Kyle Shanahan said that with so many missing players, the Niners are likely to enter Sunday's game with fewer than the maximum 48 players on the game day roster even after they make practice squad elevations on Saturday. They've had internal discussions with some of their players about further injuries forcing them to play out of position, according to Shanahan. "I don't think ever in my career (has that happened," Shanahan said. "It's a unique situation." Evans' absence creates an even greater need this week against the Falcons given the team's rash of injuries at receiver. The 49ers are already without Ricky Pearsall (knee), Samuel, De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) and Demarcus Robinson (ankle). One solution is the expected activation of veteran wideout Christian Kirk from injured reserve. The 49ers released defensive end Ogbo Okoronkwo on Friday, creating a roster spot for Kirk. While he's technically listed as questionable, Shanahan said that is procedural and Kirk is set to play against the Falcons. Kirk has been on injured reserve since the start of the season after injuring his calf in the opening days of training camp in July. Kirk said Thursday that he's felt good since returning to practice last week and was looking forward to getting back in the mix, especially considering the attrition at receiver. "Thankfully for me, I've played enough ball, I've played a lot of football and have got a lot of experience," Kirk said. "This week has just been treating every rep like a game rep... I know once I get out there on Sunday, if that's what the case is going to be, it's just like playing football again. I'm excited for that opportunity when it does present itself." With Evans sitting out this week, it gives him an extra week to deal with the Achilles tendonitis that flared up before Monday's game against the Washington Commanders . San Francisco has a Week 8 bye after Sunday in Atlanta. Before the Washington game, Evans didn't practice during the week but played and was on his way to a big performance before the Achilles flared up just before halftime. Evans did not return to the game. He was in the locker room moving slowly on specialized shoes but did not participate in practice this week. Bosa, meanwhile, had recently expressed optimism that he could return from his calf injury for the Washington or Atlanta games, but the Niners held him out of practice also, giving him additional time to recover. "I just think he was a little too optimistic, especially for Bosa because he's pretty accurate," Shanahan said. "He doesn't say stuff like that unless it's accurate. I just think it surprised him. He worked out after he said that to you guys and the next day was just a little sore, which surprised all of us and that wasn't a great sign, especially going to playing turf and stuff this week." The Niners have been without Bosa since before Week 3 against Arizona after he injured his calf during a walkthrough. San Francisco's available edge rushers against the Falcons include Mykel Williams , Romello Height , Keion White and Khalid Kareem with the possibility that Okoronkwo could re-sign to the practice squad on Saturday and elevated for Sunday against the Falcons, though the Niners also have needs at receiver and linebacker. Cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) and safety Siran Neal (neck), meanwhile, returned to practice on Friday after missing the previous two days and are questionable for Sunday.

stories.title: Falcons' viral stripes will appear down center of helmets
stories.summary: A vertical stripe pattern that the Falcons used in a social media post will appear down the middle of the team's throwback helmets. The stripes drew significant online backlash as some saw similarity to Nazi Germany imagery.
stories.detailText: FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- The Atlanta Falcons posted a rendering of their throwback logo Wednesday on social media that created an online backlash, with some posters comparing it to imagery found in Nazi Germany. The post featured the franchise's throwback black-and-white bird logo, which it used from the 1960s all the way up to the early 2000s. Behind the logo were vertical stripes in red, black and gold. The colors are a reference to the team's 1966 uniform, which consisted of a red helmet, the black Falcons logo, and black, white and gold striping on the pants. The Falcons' post remains up , but the team changed its X and Instagram profile photos to one with just the red retro helmet with the black throwback logo on it and no vertical stripes. The Falcons have worn the retro logo for games every year since 2009 with the exception of several years when the NFL prevented teams from using an alternative helmet color. Atlanta will wear the logo Sunday when it hosts the San Francisco 49ers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The presentation of the retro logo on top of the vertical striping in those colors on that specific social media post seems to be the object of controversy. The stripes will appear down the middle of the team's red helmet and not behind the logo like the graphic showed. The Falcons declined to comment on the situation. An NFL spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment from The Associated Press. Falcons owner Arthur Blank is Jewish and has donated millions to Holocaust remembrance organizations through the Molly Blank Fund, which is named after his mother. In 2023, Blank donated $1.5 million to the U.S. Holocaust Memorial Museum.

stories.title: Cowboys say still time to turn things around after 2-4 start
stories.summary: Cowboys stars Dak Prescott and CeeDee Lamb express belief that there's still time for the team to turn things around despite a 2-4 start.
stories.detailText: FRISCO, Texas -- At 2-4 and in the midst of a two-game losing streak, Dak Prescott knows it is time for the Dallas Cowboys to turn the season around. He said the mindset of the team is, "determined and I would hope urgent," entering Monday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field. "We can only say we've got a lot of games in front of us for so long. Might be already past us, right? We've got to go win," Prescott said. "You've got to go win. You want to give yourself a chance to be a winning team, to be a playoff team. You got to win as many games as you can and when you drop two games in particular games that we didn't expect to drop, it makes it that much harder. So urgent, urgent to get it done now." Despite the record, ESPN Analytics still gives the Cowboys the best chance to win the NFC East at 68%. The New York Giants are currently in first place with a 3-2-1 record but will turn to J.J. McCarthy as their starting quarterback. Like the Cowboys, the Eagles are 2-4, but will be without quarterback Jalen Hurts for the rest of the regular season due to blood clots. The Washington Commanders are in last place with a 1-4-1 record. Wide receiver CeeDee Lamb said, "Anybody can win this division, so why not us? He added, "Very fortunate that everybody else is playing pretty bad. But overall, just everything is still in front of us. We still have our opportunity to do what we want to do and that's to get in the tournament and it starts on Monday. So just shaking that back and getting back into the win column I feel like is the most important thing and that's been the point of emphasis this week." While the Cowboys defense has struggled under first-year coordinator Christian Parker -- 25th in points per game (26.5), 30th in yards (382.5), including the last ranked run defense (149.8 yards) -- the Dallas offense has hit a wall the last two weeks, scoring just 29 points. The Cowboys have not been able to sustain a running game and there has been a lack of big plays in part because of how they have handled the blitz in the last two games. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer, who serves as the playcaller, has come under criticism with an offense that was among the most accomplished last year and returned everybody in 2026. "I think it comes with the territory. I think some of it is deserved. We've got to play better. I've got to coach better," Schottenheimer said on Thursday. "When you grow up in a family that your dad's a head coach for over 20 something years, you understand that this is part of the job description. No one likes it. I block out most of it. Some of it gets to me doing this job and having to speak to you guys is part of that. But at the same time, I've got strong shoulders. "I know what a great coach I am. I know what this team is capable of, and that's what I focus on." Perhaps playing in a hostile environment on ESPN's "Monday Night Football," can help. "It's one of the few opportunities that you get that you feel like you're truly on the road, you know you're hated," Prescott said. "It's you guys and those guys on that sideline vs. the world it feels like. And that's what football's supposed to be when you go on the road and you go to someone else's house. You want that feeling. You want that atmosphere. There's nothing better than hearing them quiet or getting them to boo their team. It's just a great atmosphere. They love football up there. They expect to win and that's what makes the environment so fun and hectic."

stories.title: Cam Skattebo set to return to Giants RB mix after being 'taught a lesson'
stories.summary: After zero carries in Week 6, Cam Skattebo says he took a step back to evaluate and correct, and Giants' coach says he should return to the running back mix vs. the Texans.
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Cam Skattebo had a "good week" of practice and should return to the running back mix for the New York Giants against the Houston Texans , coach John Harbaugh said Friday. Skattebo didn't have a single carry in Sunday's 34-27 loss to the New Orleans Saints . He landed on the bench for most of last week's game after a crucial overtime fumble in a tie with the Washington Commanders . It was his fifth fumble in 13 career games. "It's been good, you know. I think I got taught a lesson," Skattebo said. "I don't know if that's from them or from myself, but I kind of had to step back and look at it and figure out why I was doing the things I was doing, what was happening. Came to practice, corrected those things, worked on them. Ready to go back out there and play ball." The Giants had Najee Harris , who was released Tuesday , Tyrone Tracy Jr. and Devin Singletary ahead of Skattebo in the rotation against the Saints. Skattebo played six snaps after averaging 42 over the first five games. The Giants praised Skattebo this week for handling it like a "pro" and trying to correct the mistakes. "He was always going to be a big part of our season," Harbaugh said. "And he had a heck of a week of practice; all the backs did." The second-year running back knows he still has to prove it on the field. "I didn't do anything yet," Skattebo said. "I took care of the ball during practice, and whatever my role is on Sunday is going to be my role and I'm going to give it everything I've got." Harbaugh said Harris' release was about setting a clearer course at running back and seemed to indicate that a four-man rotation was too much. Skattebo and Tracy are expected to split the primary role this week against a Texans defense that ranks third in the NFL against the run. Tracy worked his way back into the mix after being buried on the depth chart early this season. He had a missed block in the preseason that led to quarterback Jaxson Dart getting sent to the medical tent and fumbled in the opener. But Tracy had a receiving and a rushing touchdown in Sunday's loss to the Saints to help him earn more reps. Harbaugh talked earlier in the week about how none of the running backs have taken the reins and run with them this season. He is waiting for someone to step up. Skattebo is the team's leading rusher with 81 carries for 294 yards (3.6 YPC) with one touchdown. Giants running backs collectively have averaged 2.4 yards per carry this season. They know the pressure is on. They took notice with Harris being released. "Nobody's safe. It's as simple as that," Skattebo said. "I think when we go on the field and we perform, if we're not performing, we understand there's a possibility of not being here. If I don't perform, I know there's a possibility of me not being here. We came in this week. We continue to work. We know where we're at. We know what we have. If we put that to display, we're going to be just fine."

stories.title: Giants-Texans final injury report: Tremaine Edmunds out, Micah McFadden in
stories.summary: Giants get good news on the offensive line.
stories.detailText: Tremaine Edmunds | Getty Images The New York Giants will be without starting inside linebacker Tremaine Edmunds this Sunday against the Houston Texans. Edmunds has a torn chest muscle and that injury that will reportedly end his season . The good news for the Giants is that starting offensive tackles Andrew Thomas (groin) and Jermaine Eluemunor (calf), and backup tackle Marcus Mbow (knee) are all expected to play. McFadden ready for opportunity With Edmunds out, fifth-year linebacker and former starter Micah McFadden will get the starting nod. “If I get to go out there and play and start and do what I’ve gotten to do before, I’m excited,” McFadden told Big Blue View earlier this week. McFadden was a full-time starter for the Giants in 2023 and 2024. In Game 1 last season, McFadden suffered a foot injury that kept him out for the remainder of the season. He admitted that “without a doubt” it isn’t easy to no longer have a starting role. “Whenever you’re used to something, you’ve had a taste of the pie, I guess, and then you don’t get to go out there and eat with your boys anymore, it’s tough, but I think it’s just about staying present,” McFadden said. “This game is a week-to-week basis, and obviously I had a pretty upsetting first week last year, and I learned a lot through that process, though. A lot of gratitude to be healthy and just to be able to play again, and I think that’s what I found most throughout these past six weeks is just, just finding gratitude in whatever situation I’m in.” At least for this week, McFadden will be starting again. Could he also be wearing the green dot, relaying defensive calls from coordinator Dennard Wilson? “I’ve done it before, and I think Dennard knows that there’s a handful of guys that could all do this on our defense,” McFadden said. “Whether I am that guy or not I’ll be prepared for it. I’m glad that I have had experience doing it in the past just to, you know, so this wouldn’t be my first time. “Obviously if that opportunity presents itself, it’s something I would take pride in and make sure I’m communicating with everybody.” Adebo appears set to return The Giants designated cornerback Paulson Adebo to return this week, and it looks like he could be activated before Sunday’s game. “He’s ready to go,” Harbaugh said. “He’s a legit corner. He’s a cover corner, he tackles. He’s been a high-end corner in this league. I think he’s really determined to play that way. I think he’s finally probably healthy and ready to go. I can’t wait to see it … it looks like it’s going to be Sunday.” With starting cornerback Greg Newsome II still in concussion protocol and ruled out, there could be immediate snaps for Adebo vs. the Texans. stories.title: The Colts Have More Paths to a Bright Future Than You Think
stories.summary: The Colts have a lot of possibilities to rebuild this roster quickly, and that’s an exciting thing for this franchise
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS, IN - OCTOBER 18: Carlie Irsay-Gordon co-owner and CEO of the Indianapolis Colts instructs fans the the Adam Venturi banner that was reviled at half time during and NFL game between the Tennessee Titans and the Indianapolis Colts on October 18, 2026 at Lucas Oil Stadium at Indianapolis, IN. (Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Colts finally did it. I think by now, anyone clicking on this article doesn’t need a full autopsy of the Chris Ballard era. I intentionally wait to do these long form pieces, because I like to take the emotion out of my analysis. However, when it comes to the end Chris Ballard era, there isn’t much analysis needed. It was time, and anyone who followed the team realized it. You didn’t have to listen closely to hear the “Fire Ballard!” chants echoing throughout Lucas Oil Stadium during the team’s annual humiliating loss, this time to the winless Titans. While it was obvious, that this was going to be an end of the Chris Ballard era, one thing is certain: This is one of the most complex and nuanced tenures of any GM in NFL history. The reality is that there were numerous exits the Colts could have taken. 2021, certainly 2022, and 2024 all come to mind. Like a cat, Chris Ballard had 9 lives. If it wasn’t the epic choke in 2021 that caused the Colts to miss the playoffs, it had to be the year an ESPN analyst took over as head coach in one of the most embarrassing seasons in franchise history. After all that turmoil, surely he wouldn’t survive a season in which his handpicked quarterback tapped out of a game and was benched, while a team captain handed opponents free bulletin board material on his podcast, only for the Giants to whoop the Colts with a backup quarterback and end their season… Right? Wrong. Because the Chris Ballard tenure was never assessed on paper. He endured one of most shocking retirements in NFL history, which we all know by now. But also judging from some of the reporting, the health of late owner Jim Irsay played a role in his retention. It was more than the mediocre seasons and rosters with holes that the fanbase could identify in August. The Colts were loyal to him for as long as they possibly could be. That’s the gist of the story every Colts fan knows by now, perhaps all too well. But now that Chris Ballard has been fired, the Colts are closing a significant chapter in their franchise’s history and are grabbing the pen to start writing the next one. The funny part is that some people have already written it for them. There’s a narrative that the Colts are hosting a firesale, similar to what the Miami Dolphins did after firing Chris Grier around this time last year. Mock trades are flooding your social media feeds, with teams hoping to compete for a Lombardi Trophy raiding the Colts’ roster for just about every talented player they have. However, this is nothing like the 2025 Miami Dolphins. WHERE DO THE COLTS GO FROM HERE? This is may sound crazy to a portion of an understandably livid fanbase, but the first order of business has to be continuing to compete this year. And it’s a real possibility that they do. In the NFL, it’s fairly easy to see when teams are waving the white flag. You can see it in the press conferences and you can see it on the sidelines on Sundays. It’s pretty obvious. Typically, a coach is then fired. But the Colts didn’t fire a coach, they fired their GM. Carlie Irsay-Gordon is sending a message to everyone in that building that it’s time to wake up. Shane Steichen, Lou Anarumo, Daniel Jones, and the rest of the roster.. If they didn’t realize it already, they certainly realize it now. Everyone is playing and coaching for their jobs. The Colts can use this as an opportunity to roll over like they always have, or they can jumpstart their season and continue to keep fighting. The good news about having an owner that’s intimately involved with the organization? She gets a front row seat to see who quits on this team. Those are the people you can guarantee won’t be here next year. Maybe the roster was so poorly constructed that they’ll never be able to compete this season, but watch them this Sunday. I bet they show you some fight. 2026 FIRESALE? Circling back to the aforementioned firesale that everyone is convinced is about to occur. Ed Dodds, and certainly Carlie Irsay-Gordon, are going to do their due diligence to move some of the players that were never going to be apart of the team’s future this year. I think we can conclude that DeForest Buckner will eventually be one of those people. He’s on the last year of an expiring deal, is 32 years old, and wants to win. It’s about as natural a parting of ways as you’ll find in the NFL. He knows it, we know it, and 31 other teams know it. It would shock me to see him on the roster come mid-November. But everyone else? I’m not so sure. Like I said, the Colts are trying to win still. If they upset the undefeated Vikings, don’t things look a lot different? A win can do so much for a team in the NFL. Now I think we can be realistic to say that is still pretty unlikely. The Colts’ roster has plenty of flaws, as we’ve discussed all season, but that doesn’t mean the team should start trading away its best players. They would be wise to hold on to anyone who could still have a future with the franchise. That includes Jonathan Taylor, Quenton Nelson and Josh Downs. Is there a price for everyone? Of course. A massive overpay could completely change the equation. Just look at the Jets last year. But ask yourself this: Why would the Colts want to part ways with players that a potential new GM might view as building blocks for the future? You owe that the new GM to make that decision for himself. IS THIS AN ATTRACTIVE JOB? If you had asked me this question in January, I would have said no. Without a first-round pick and with an unsettled QB situation, I assumed they might be in stuck until they paid off the debts of the Sauce Gardner trade. But I underestimated one thing: The owner. I think Carlie Irsay-Gordon is a massive reason to take the job. Why? Because she’s deeply committed to process over results. She’s deeply invested in the team. And she’s willing to do what it takes to win. Also if you’re a GM taking over this job, are the standards If you zoom out to when she took over last year, it’s been quite the ride. The Colts were one of the hottest teams in the NFL, and while I did not agree with the move, she let Chris Ballard mortgage their future at the deadline to try and win. And then when things didn’t work out, she gave him a second chance. That goes a long way. Despite having quality ownership in your corner, it’s undeniable that the resources the Colts have to work with are probably not going to earn them the top job on the market this offseason. They don’t have the ammo to get a blue-chip prospect and they don’t have a QB that will entice many candidates to want to build a team around. That being said, while the roster might have some flaws, it can get better in a hurry. THE COLTS PATH MOVING FORWARD I’m positive that the Colts are going to get differing opinions in GM interviews about the state of the roster. Some people are going to love the young talent that’s on the roster and want to build around it. Others will look at an aging core that hasn’t accomplished anything and see an opportunity to sell high on its veterans and want to get younger quickly. Both give me a sense for optimism. While I don’t have a crystal ball, I really believe things can get better in Indianapolis quickly. Things in the NFL change fast and all it takes is one good offseason to completely change the trajectory of your team. Look at the 2024 Eagles who added Saquon Barkley and reinvented their secondary in the first two rounds of the draft. Look at the 2025 Seahawks who completely tore down their offense to the studs and built it all the way back up. The past guarantees nothing for the Colts moving forward, but it does offer something that fans are desperate for. Hope. Let’s examine both paths: PATH #1: A RE-TOOLING The first path is the new GM wanting to build on the foundation that Ballard and Steichen have already set. epending on how the Colts finish the season, Steichen could even be retained under this scenario. Indianapolis has had talent on its roster for years, but an unsettled quarterback situation and an inability to strike the right balance between drafting well and supplementing the roster through free agency have consistently held the team back. A new GM could continue building the defense through the draft while using the Colts’ projected $67 million in 2027 cap space to add the finishing touches to the roster. The Colts would also get Alec Pierce back, which could be transformational for the offense. Combine his return with the young core already in place and a few key veteran additions (perhaps at wide receiver) and Indianapolis could find itself right back in the mix. The Colts will have a big decision to make at Quarterback in either route the new GM will take. Will he decline to take the dead money on Daniel Jones’ contract and give him another year removed from his achilles injury to find his groove again under Steichen? Doesn’t sound appealing to anyone reading, but certainly an option. Could the Colts use any DeForest Buckner ammunition to take a QB in the 2nd round and have a Wentz/Hurts situation? Definitely could. Quarterback will remain the biggest question mark, but I still believe the 2026 season has become about more than Jones, even if he contributed to many of the team’s early struggles. With the proper supporting cast and structure around him, I think he can still return to form. PATH #2: THE REBUILD There will be candidates who look at this roster and want nothing to do with it. They may not want to pay a guard market-setting money, build an offense around a running back entering his third contract with plenty of carries under his belt, or commit to young players whose evaluations don’t align with theirs. Would that lead to a Miami Dolphins-type season? I still say no. People seem to forget how much dead money Miami had to incur when moving on from Tua Tagovailoa. His massive contract forced the Dolphins into significant rebuild. The Colts don’t have that same problem. If a new GM wanted to trade Jonathan Taylor and collect comp picks by letting players like Quenton Nelson and Josh Downs walk in free agency, those options would be available. Would that improve Indianapolis’ chances of competing in 2027? Absolutely not. But even in that scenario, the Colts wouldn’t be facing the same uphill battle Miami did. They have more financial flexibility, more young talent to build around and more flexibility in how they want to reshape the roster. A new GM could bring in his own players to fit what would likely be a new head coach’s scheme while still building a solid foundation for the future, with an eye toward 2028. The quarterback situation in this scenario could get complicated. The Colts could release Daniel Jones and absorb the dead money, but I also wonder whether another team would be willing to trade for him. The league has generally been higher on Jones than the public has. Tom Pelissero floated the possibility on The Ringer Show , and the more I’ve thought about it, the more I believe it’s a possibility. Minnesota and Kevin O’Connell have valued Jones in the past, and the Vikings aren’t necessarily tied to Kyler Murray long-term. Their offense has also struggled at times this season, despite the team’s record. A trade isn’t impossible to imagine. Moving Jones would give the Colts an opportunity to reset at quarterback while allowing a new regime to build around a fresh roster, one that might look different but wouldn’t necessarily be less talented. Ultimately, it’s hard to envision Carlie Irsay-Gordon signing off on the kind of full-scale rebuild that fans and national media have suggested. She wants to win, not endure on a lengthy rebuilding process. And there’s little reason to believe Indianapolis needs to tear everything down to build a successful team. BOTTOM LINE The Colts have plenty of questions to answer over the next 365 days. Some will be tougher than others, and the answers will likely vary depending on which candidate you ask. But I think a lot of possibilities remain on the table, and that’s an exciting thing for this franchise. Despite what the popular narrative that exists, the Colts aren’t backed into a corner. I’ve laid out two big-picture paths the new GM could take, but the reality will likely fall somewhere in between, blending elements of both approaches. For the first time in a decade, Indianapolis is on the verge of a fresh start. The organization finally has a chance to ascend instead of desperately clinging to a league-average roster and selling fans on the promise of something more. Carlie Irsay-Gordon means business, and she just proved it to the entire NFL.

stories.title: NFL admits a penalty by the Cowboys in Week 5 was assessed against the Bucs
stories.summary: The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off th…
stories.detailText: The NFL has admitted a rather embarrassing officiating mistake from Week 5: When Buccaneers defensive lineman Calijah Kancey was called for illegal hands to the face, it was actually a Cowboys player who put his hands in Kancey's face, and somehow the wrong team got assessed the penalty when it was time to step off the yardage. In the weekly officiating video , NFL officiating and rules analyst Walt Anderson said Cowboys guard Tyler Booker put his hands in Kancey's face but somehow that was miscommunicated as Kancey committing the penalty. Anderson said when the on-field officials make a mistake that blatant, the league officiating office should correct it immediately. "Were going to have a foul called on No. 94 on the defensive team for illegal hands to the face," Anderson said. "The only action relative to any hands is really by the offensive player here. So this is the type of play that the Competition Committee has instructed officiating that if objective information in terms of just asking the officials, 'Are we sure we have the right number of the player here?' that we can end up assisting with this. Because it's clearly not a foul by No. 94. If there is illegal use of hands, it's obviously by No. 52 of the offense." Kancey made clear in the moment that he knew it was a bad call, but there's nothing a player can do to fix a bad call against him. The New York officiating office could have fixed it, but didn't.

stories.title: Ravens' Lamar Jackson (high ankle sprain) unsure if he'll play
stories.summary: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson said he's dealing with a high ankle sprain and is unsure if he'll play this week against the Bengals, but is "heading in the right direction" after missing the past two games.
stories.detailText: OWINGS MILLS, Md. -- After walking with a limp to the podium after Friday's practice, Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson expressed uncertainty whether he will play Sunday against the Cincinnati Bengals , saying his decision will come down to pain tolerance. "Right now, I'm heading in the right direction," said Jackson, who is officially listed as questionable. "I can't call it right now." Jackson said that he is dealing with a high ankle sprain, which he suffered in a win over the Tennessee Titans 19 days ago. He indicated the swelling has gone down significantly, but he is still experiencing pain in his injured left ankle and foot. The two-time NFL Most Valuable Player doesn't believe he needs to be at 100% to suit up for Sunday's important AFC North game between the Ravens (4-2) and Bengals (3-2). "If I can just go out there and feel the pain a little bit, I can play," Jackson said. "But if I'm restricted and I can't do what I do, I'm not helping nobody. If I can just go out there and just be a statue and get hit, that's not helping my team at all." If Jackson can't play, the Ravens will start Tyler Huntley for a third straight week. There has been increased hope surrounding Jackson after he returned to practice with limited participation all week. He was not seen walking off the field with the rest of the team at the end of Friday's practice, but Ravens coach Jesse Minter mentioned that Jackson "was able to get a pretty good amount of work in." It's looking like a game-time decision with Jackson. "I think it's in that phase where we'll certainly go as long as it needs to take," Minter said on when the team will make a decision at starting quarterback. On Oct. 4, Jackson was injured on the last offensive snap before halftime, when he was sacked from behind. It looked like Titans defensive end Jermaine Johnson II 's shoulder landed on the outside of Jackson's left ankle, which caused it to bend awkwardly. "It was very, very, very, very, very painful," Jackson said. After getting treatment every day and repeatedly icing the ankle, Jackson felt he turned the corner Sunday, when Baltimore was playing at Cleveland . He ran "a little bit" Sunday and Monday before resuming practice Wednesday. Jackson doesn't feel pain when he walks, but he does at practice when he tries to plant his foot. "It's just like trying to run ... can't put too much pressure [on the left foot]," Jackson said. It was around this time last season, when Jackson missed three games with a hamstring injury. On Friday, he expressed regret rushing back from it because he was never truly healthy the rest of the season. "I feel like that was dumb a little bit because I was still hurting," Jackson said. "I'm trying to help my team win, but I'm not to my full capability or not even close to it." The Ravens' offense has struggled with its consistency without Jackson. In 14 quarters with Jackson this season, the Ravens have scored 116 points and 14 offensive touchdowns. In 10 quarters with Huntley, Baltimore has totaled 40 points and four touchdowns. If Jackson can play Sunday, it would be a timely return. Since Jackson became the starter midway through the 2018 season, the Ravens are 11-2 against the Bengals with Jackson, who has thrown 24 touchdowns and six interceptions against Cincinnati. Without Jackson over that span, Baltimore is 0-3, including the playoffs, against the Bengals, losing by an average margin of 12 points. "One thing I'll say about Lamar is that he's super competitive and he wants to play," Minter said. "It's going to be a decision based on how he feels and how effective he feels like he can be and how we feel like it looks."

The 30-24 loss at Soldier Field marked the first appearances of 2026 for the offensive lineman as well as the outside linebacker. Newman-Johnson, 27, made his Thursday night debut in protection on three extra points and one field goal. The 6-foot-2, 297-pound interior lineman provided depth behind a starting five that was missing right guard Ben Brown due to a knee injury and also lost left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker to injured reserve ahead of the 8:15 p.m. ET kickoff due to a hamstring injury . Added to New England’s practice squad in September after being hosted on a visit, Newman-Johnson now stands 26 games into his NFL career. First entering the league with head coach Mike Vrabel’s former Tennessee Titans as an undrafted free agent in 2022, the Baylor product spent parts of two seasons in the AFC South. He went on to reside on the New York Jets’ practice squad, 53-man roster and injured reserve before being released and landing in Foxborough. A five-game starter, his odometer includes 338 downs on offense and 72 downs in the kicking game. Whitley, 27, handled 13 snaps on special teams during the Midwest road trip between kickoff coverage, kickoff return and punt return. That marked 46 percent of the workload in the transitional phase. The well-traveled edge rusher signed to the Patriots’ practice squad in September. A Massachusetts native and Holy Cross alum, Whitley originally entered the NFL with the Los Angeles Rams as part of the organization’s undrafted class of 2022. He went on to make stops with the Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings, New York Giants, Arizona Cardinals and Tampa Bay Buccaneers through 2025. And his most recent training camp was spent with the Cleveland Browns before being waived at the league’s cutdown deadline at the end of August. Seven games into his career, the 6-foot-4, 255-pound linebacker has recorded one fumble recovery and one pass defensed through 16 snaps on defense and 87 snaps on special teams. stories.title: Commanders projected to sell offensive lineman at NFL trade deadline
stories.summary: ESPN reporter Bill Barnwell believes Washington Commanders will trade offensive lineman Andrew Wylie to the Patriots
stories.detailText: The NFL trade deadline is coming up in the relatively near future, with the last day to deal on Nov. 10. That comes right after a Week 9 contest with the L.A. Rams, after which we should have a great idea about this Commanders season. Washington must surge and stack some wins right away, lest the season go south. Will the Commander be buyers or sellers at the trade deadline? That will depend on what happens next. We’ll see tons of projected trades in the coming weeks, and ESPN believes Washington general manager Adam Peters could make a minor move to add a asset. Bill Barnwell has the Commanders dealing from their offensive line depth, parting with a versatile chess piece with some serious experience for a Day 3 pick. The deal: Andrew Wylie gets sent to the Commanders for a 2027 sixth-round pick. Here’s Barnwell’s explanation for why this deal works for both sides: “It’s rare to see a team nearly run out of linemen in an NFL game, but the Patriots came close last week. With Mike Onwenu already sidelined and Will Campbell playing despite a knee injury , New England lost Alijah Vera-Tucker , Morgan Moses and Ben Brown during a win over the Jets , leaving the defending AFC champs with a mere five healthy offensive linemen. The line made it through the rest of the contest, and Moses could be back this week, but the Patriots are remarkably thin up front. Adding a versatile lineman to the mix makes a lot of sense. Wylie can play right tackle or either guard spot, allowing him to fill in across the lineup with relative ease. He’s buried on the Commanders’ depth chart and has played just 15 snaps this season despite the absence of left tackle Laremy Tunsil , which caused Brandon Coleman to move to the left side. With multiple sixth-round picks, the Patriots can afford to ship one off to add a veteran. And the Commanders could turn to practice-squaders Trent Scott or Esa Pole , who filled in for the Chiefs at left tackle last season, as their swing tackle after Wylie’s departure.” This isn’t a major deal, but would you make it? Also, do you think the Commanders should add talent or sell off even more pieces of this roster? Let us know in the article comments below.
