stories.title: 'Football 301' takes closer look at Chiefs vs. Seahawks, the Kenneth Walker III revenge game
stories.summary: "I kind of think he wants to come in here and have a big game against the team that pretty much just said, 'Thanks for winning us that Super Bowl… we're going to give your money to Rashid Shaheed'"
stories.detailText: One of Week 7's most anticipated matchups unfolds on prime time as the Seattle Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football. While this game could have playoff implications, the biggest storyline centers around Chiefs running back Kenneth Walker III's return to the Pacific Northwest to face his old team. Here's how the " Football 301 " podcast crew of Nate Tice and Matt Harmon sees this matchup playing out on Sunday. What to expect from Walker's return to Seattle After an offseason that saw the Seahawks make a controversial decision to let Super Bowl MVP Walker walk in free agency, the Chiefs pounced, handing the explosive playmaker a backfield all to himself. Walker has swiftly become the "identity force" in Kansas City, revitalizing a Chiefs run game that had long struggled for consistency and big plays. During the Football 301 podcast, the emotional and strategic angles were not lost. "Sometimes the Revenge Game stuff is nonsense," Harmon said. "I kind of think he wants to come in here and have a big game against the team that pretty much just said, 'Thanks for winning us that Super Bowl… we're going to give your money to Rashid Shaheed'" Despite Kansas City coaches' comments to the contrary, Walker's workload has been heavy. He has 106 carries for an NFL-leading 665 yards and six touchdowns, along with two receiving TDs. Good on good: elite offense vs. elite defense On paper, the game promises classic strength-on-strength. Kansas City's offense, first in both yards per play and success rate, goes up against a Seahawks defense ranked first in both explosive plays and yards per play allowed. Chiefs QB Patrick Mahomes appears to be in peak form, making big throws, improvising under pressure and enabling a receiving corps that, while not loaded with stars, features a blend of vertical threats and physical role players. Tight end Travis Kelce's impact remains high both as a receiver and as a blocker, giving the Chiefs versatility to attack Seattle multiple ways. Seattle's defense, led by creative play-caller Mike Macdonald, enjoys a deep line rotation and formidable secondary. Their ability to limit explosive plays and force offenses into inefficiency has been a hallmark, setting up an intriguing chess match between two of the NFL's brightest minds in Macdonald and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid. How will Seattle respond? For the Seahawks, the question is whether their defense can keep Walker in check and slow a surging Kansas City attack. "If you can get this Seahawks defense in any ways… sometimes running backs in the passing game [are the answer]," the podcast highlighted. On the flip side, the crew noted the Seahawks' offense is hampered by a struggling run game and a lack of complementary weapons for Jaxon Smith-Njigba. Defenses have heavily clouded and bracketed him, daring Seattle to win elsewhere. The Chiefs' defense, meanwhile, excels at bracketing top receivers and will likely try to take away JSN, forcing someone else to step up. QB Sam Darnold's struggles under pressure and against man coverage were cited as a vulnerability for Seattle — particularly with Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo dialing up exotic blitzes. Prediction Both analysts expect the game to tilt toward the Chiefs due to their offensive versatility and the Seahawks' challenges in finding secondary offensive contributors. If the Chiefs' offense is neutralized by the Seahawks' D, the Chiefs' defense still holds advantages against a one-dimensional Seattle attack. The recipe for Seattle to pull the upset would require new wrinkles from their offensive coaching staff — something there's little indication of so far.

teamStories.summary: The Rams may be 4.5 favorites; however, this game feels like the Patriots game, but at home for the Las Vegas Raiders.
teamStories.detailText: . (Eric Thayer / Los Angeles Times via Getty Images) Decimated by injuries and with a 2-4 record, the Los Angeles Rams have fallen far from being the Super Bowl favorites initially thought. Currently cellar-dwelling in the depths of the NFC West once again proving that “dream teams” are just a dream. All signs point to this being a very winnable game in Week 7 for the Las Vegas Raiders. Precisely why Raider Nation and head coach Klint Kubiak should be concerned. Against the New England Patriots, missing four defensive backs and #1 wide receiver A.J. Brown, and with a host of banged-up players, the Raiders were soundly beaten 45-17. To be fair, they were also coming off a close, emotional loss with a comeback bid falling just short to Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. Sounds kinda familiar, doesn’t it? This week, after a 33-30 loss to Josh Allen and the Buffalo Bills, the Raiders have a chance to right the ship against a reeling Rams team and exorcise some demons. The Rams team, without Myles Garrett, recently placed the following players on injured reserve: Davante Adams, Poona Ford, Kobie Turner, and Blake Grupe, the replacement kicker. Nate Scheelhase, the Rams offensive coordinator, is experiencing some first-year coordinator growing pains. Last year under Mike Lafleur, the Rams had the number-one scoring and yardage offense; this year they have fallen all the way to 20th in scoring offense. Revisionist history on can’t-lose games hasn’t been kind to the Raiders. Whether it’s head coaches who have never coached before or quarterbacks who have been on the team for less than a week, or rosters missing 50% of their starters, these games never seem to work out for the Raiders. Concerns or sports fans masochism s Aaron Donald has yet to make the impact many thought he would coming out of retirement. Against the Raiders’ left side of the offensive line, which is their worst, he could finally get right. Spencer Burford has struggled mightily to block anyone who wasn’t a lower-caliber player; Tyler Linderbaum hasn’t been as good as advertised, nor has he played up to the contract he was awarded. Kolton Miller is getting pumped up by analytics charts from whoever is using AI to draw them up. When, in fact, his play has bordered on abysmal. Braden Fisk is facing a right guard situation where the position no longer has an entrenched starter. For as much as Kubiak has said there will be competition at the position, no player, be it Jackson Powers-Johnson or Caleb Rogers, has seized control. Rogers missed some key blocks last week and was blown up in a short-yardage situation, which ended a drive inside the red zone and under the shadow of the goalposts. Schematically, no teams deploy 13 personnel (one back, three tight ends) more than the Raiders’ current and last opponents. The Rams rank 1st at 29% of their offense and the Bills rank 2nd at 27%; realistically, that means a heavy emphasis on the run game and a lack of talent at the wide receiver position. The Rams have rushed for 676 yards, six rushing touchdowns and average 4.6 yards per carry. Ranking 12th in the NFL through six games. Too much to cover Covering tight ends continues to be a work in progress for the Raiders defense. Safeties Treydan Stukes and Jeremy Chinn continue to be up and down in terms of communication and execution. Stukes being the expected weakest link. Stukes, a rookie safety, struggles with in-breaking routes run by big ol’ tight ends. Chinn, the veteran, struggles with the out-breaking routes and lacks the twitch or long speed to keep up. Throwing in a third tight end puts a linebacker (Quay Walker or Nakobe Dean) on them, sometimes Taron Johnson, or leaves them open to a soft vacated zone. While the Raiders’ pass defense has prepared itself for wide receiver-heavy offenses, the tight ends and the running backs out of the backfield have been the Achilles’ heel. What’s problematic is that this plays right into Scheelhase’s and quarterback Matthew Stafford’s hands. Stafford has been without either Adams or Puka Nacua in every game except the game in Australia in Week 1 and last week. So sticking with power sets and standing tall in the pocket waiting to throw to tight ends and running backs is nothing new to him. Ultimately, it will be up to the Raiders’ offense to take advantage of the injuries to the Rams’ defense to get the win in Las Vegas, but the defense will have to be even better at getting to the quarterback and getting him on the ground. If not the song and dance of “the same old Raiders” will get louder and start to become unbearable.

teamStories.title: Rams could be reason Raiders turn to Fernando Mendoza
teamStories.summary: 5 Qs, 5 As with Silver and Black Pride
teamStories.detailText: Kirk Cousins leads the NFL in touchdown passes with 14, and started his career with the Las Vegas Raiders at 3-0, but the veteran signal caller is playing with fire amid a three-game losing streak. If the Raiders lose to the spiraling Los Angeles Rams on Sunday, the fans begging to see number one pick Fernando Mendoza take the reins could finally get their wish. It’s not necessarily because Cousins lost the job, but that he was always just keeping it warm for Mendoza. In fact, Cousins has played so well this season that Las Vegas should be able to flip him before the trade deadline for a draft pick. Perhaps on his way back to the Minnesota Vikings? The Las Vegas Raiders might have to make a tough decision heading into Week 7. https://t.co/LjdhJRguey — Raider Nation (@RaidersNationCP) October 21, 2026 That was one of the topics that came up in this weeks 5 Qs with Silver and Black Pride’s Matt Holder. I asked about the season that Cousins is having and what it means for Mendoza, and his answer pulled no punches: “At that point, it might be time to start thinking about 2027 and beyond because the team isn’t winning despite the 38-year-old quarterback playing well.” Under any other circumstances, the Raiders would be thanking their lucky stars for Cousins. The carousel has been a nightmare since Derek Carr was cut and went to the Saints. But despite his 14 touchdowns, Cousins is starting to just get in the way, it seems. Q: Is Kirk Cousins all the way back to being Kirk Cousins, or do you think he’s just had a nice setup so far and Fernando Mendoza will take over this season? A: Cousins has definitely played a lot better than I (and most people) expected. It helps that he has experience working with Klint Kubiak, since they spent three years together in Minnesota when Gary Kubiak was the Vikings offensive coordinator (2019-2020), and Klint was the quarterbacks coach (2019-2020) and took over as OC in 2021. During the preseason, it was clear that Cousins has command of the offense/system, and that has continued over the last six weeks. The Raiders come into this game ranking sixth in points per game (27.0) and seventh in passing yards per game (263.5). However, as you alluded to, the veteran signal caller is keeping the seat warm for Mendoza. Cousins has played well enough to make the Raiders a surprise playoff contender in the first half of the campaign, likely extending his time as the starter. And even during the three-game losing streak, he’s far from the team’s biggest problem and is a big reason they’ve been competitive in two out of the three losses. But the fact of the matter is that Las Vegas hasn’t beaten a quality opponent, and the October losses have made September feel like more of a fluke. If the Raiders lose this week, that’ll be four in a row and their record will dip below .500 for the first time this year. At that point, it might be time to start thinking about 2027 and beyond because the team isn’t winning despite the 38-year-old quarterback playing well. So, even though the decision would have nothing to do with Cousins’ performance, turning to the rookie to give him experience and start building for the future will likely become Kubiak’s and the organization’s priority. Q: Tre Tucker could be one of the more shocking fourth-year breakout receivers of recent memory. What makes him so good and do you expect his production to continue long-term? A: The 2023 third-round pick has been getting better and more productive every year despite working with subpar quarterbacks. For example, Tucker was the Raiders’ leading receiver with 57 catches, 696 yards and five touchdowns last year, all of which were career highs. He came into the league as a deep threat, and that’s still his bread and butter, but he’s grown tremendously as a route runner to be a threat in the intermediate areas of the field as well. So, I’m not surprised that Tucker is starting to climb up the receiver charts and get more recognition this season, ranking 20th in the NFL with 371 receiving yards through six weeks. He’s a good second option behind Brock Bowers in the passing game and has been the only wide receiver on the roster who has been productive this year. That being said, the long-term production question is tough to answer because the fourth-year pro is in a contract year. It will be interesting to see what his market looks like because his production has typically come in spurts rather than being consistent game-by-game, making it difficult to determine if he’s a go-to target moving forward. Q: I don’t know anything about defensive coordinator Rob Leonard. Tell me about him. A: Leonard was hired as the Raiders’ defensive line coach during Josh McDaniels’ second and final season as head coach. He had worked with defensive coordinator Patrick Graham — who he replaced this past offseason — for several years prior to landing in Las Vegas. Last year, Leonard’s role expanded by adding defensive run game coordinator to his title, and the defense showed a few impressive run blitzes and stunts that helped create negative plays in the running game throughout the season. When Klint Kubiak took over, what likely helped the former defensive line coach stay with the Raiders and receive a promotion is that he spent one year under current Seattle Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald when Macdonald was the Baltimore Ravens’ defensive coordinator. Obviously, Kubiak is tied to the Seahawks’ head coach too, having won a Super Bowl together last February. It seems pretty clear that Kubiak wanted to run a variation of Macdonald’s defense in Vegas, which is what Leonard is doing. The first-time coordinator has continued to develop the blitzes and stunts that he used in the run game last year, expanding them with simulated pressures, creeper blitzes and safety rotations to defend against the passing attack. Vegas’ defense has a lot of moving parts that can create confusion for quarterbacks and lead to turnovers — they had nine in the first three games — but that also can be a determinant. Leonard’s tendacies have been exposed during the three-game losing streak, as the Chiefs and Patriots routinely had the perfect play call for the Raiders’ defense. That was a little better last week, but the unit is very reliant on taking the ball away, and getting just one turnover in the last three weeks has led to them allowing 108 points during that time frame. At the end of the day, Leonard is still learning how to be an effective play-caller, and it doesn’t help that he doesn’t have that much talent to work with. Q: Who is one player on the Raiders defense that’s an absolute baller but the majority of NFL fans haven’t heard of him before? As mentioned above, Vegas’ defense doesn’t have enough talent outside of Maxx Crosby, who everyone has heard of at this point. So, this is a tough question to answer, but the first name that comes to mind is linebacker Nakobe Dean. Granted, Dean was fairly well-known as a draft prospect coming out of Georgia and spent the last four seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, meaning he’s far from a “no-name”. But he fits the criteria the best because he hasn’t received any Pro Bowls or postseason recognition and is all of the field on the Raiders’ defense. The former Eagle has made several impact plays against the run, routinely coming up with big third-down stops in key moments of the game. Within that, he’s tied for the NFL lead with three forced fumbles, all of which have come in the fourth quarter with less than four minutes left on the clock. Q: Give the Offensive Line a letter grade and tell me if you think they’re trending up or down this week. C-. Tyler Linderbaum signed a historic contract in free agency that makes him the highest-paid center by $9 million per year, but he has only been above-average and not the Top 5 player at the position the Raiders thought they were getting. Left Tackle Kolton Miller has been solid but isn’t nearly the pass protector he was in the past. Those were the two veteran linemen most people, including myself, were counting on to be the reliable presence in the trenches and help elevate the group as a whole. However, that hasn’t been the case. Guard Spencer Burford is inconsistent at best, as he’s gone back and forth between being bad and good from week to week. At the other guard spot, Jackson Powers-Johnson beat out Caleb Rogers in training camp to be the starter in the first four games he played in. However, Powers-Johnson has also been inconsistent, leading to Rogers replacing him last week. The latter had an okay showing against the Bills but really struggled when facing defensive tackle Deone Walker, who has been on a tear to begin the season. Meanwhile, the only pleasant surprise on the Raiders offensive line has been right tackle DJ Glaze, who has dramatically improved after being one of the worst pass-blocking offensive tackles in the NFL last year. But the offense still can’t run the ball because running backs Ashton Jeanty and Mike Washington Jr. don’t have consistent holes, and the pass protection isn’t good enough for a 38-year-old quarterback who can’t move and navigate the pocket. Mendoza could help improve the latter, but Vegas certainly needs to get more out of the trenches moving forward.

teamStories.detailText: Rams wide receiver Puka Nacua warms up before facing the Arizona Cardinals at SoFi Stadium on Oct. 18. (Harry How / Getty Images) Rams receiver Puka Nacua did not practice Friday because of a calf injury and was listed as questionable for Sunday’s game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Nacua took part in the majority of practice on Thursday but did not finish it. Rams coach Sean McVay indicated that tests revealed “a little minor thing in there,” and that Nacua would be a game-time decision Sunday. “I don’t think he knows exactly when it occurred,” McVay said, adding, “he felt it where he wasn’t able to have some of the power and full explosion ... but I don’t think he was aware of any sort of specific play that led to it.” Read more: How a clash between Inglewood leaders and SoFi Stadium operators hit the ballot Nacua played in the season-opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers and then sat out two games because of a hip injury that caused abdominal soreness. He returned and produced more than 100 yards receiving in each of the next two games, and then caught six passes for 80 yards in Sunday’s 18-16 defeat by the Arizona Cardinals. Nacua, the NFL receptions leader in 2025, has 37 catches for 417 yards and a touchdown, and he also has rushed for a touchdown this season. Nacua’s injury is the latest in a series suffered by a Rams team that opened the season as the favorite to win Super Bowl LXI at SoFi Stadium , but has lost its last two games to fall to 2-4. Receiver Davante Adams is expected to be sidelined six to 10 weeks because of a hamstring injury suffered against the Cardinals. Rams CB Trent McDuffie working with training staff. He is questionable for game against Raiders. pic.twitter.com/993xUzHHPT — Gary Klein (@LATimesklein) October 23, 2026 Jordan Whittington, Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell and rookie CJ Daniels are other Rams receivers. “It’s our job to figure out, all right, what are some of the spots we can put them in that accentuate their skill sets,” McVay said. Inside linebacker Nate Landman is out because of a concussion, McVay said. So veteran Eric Kendricks, who was signed to the practice squad a few weeks ago, will be activated to the roster against the Raiders. Cornerback Trent McDuffie , who sat out against the Cardinals because of a groin injury, did not practice this week and will be listed as questionable against the Raiders.
